'''''Plagiomnium cuspidatum''''', also known as '''toothed''' or '''"baby-tooth" ''plagiomnium'' moss''' and '''woodsy thyme-moss''', is a species of thyme-moss that originated in North America, but can now also be found throughout Middle America, Africa, Northern and Southern Asia (excluding China), and Europe.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tropicos {{!}} Name - !Plagiomnium cuspidatum (Hedw.) T.J. Kop. |url=http://legacy.tropicos.org/Name/35168750?tab=distribution |access-date=2020-03-04 |website=legacy.tropicos.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=ITIS - Report: Plagiomnium cuspidatum |url=https://www.itis.gov/servlet/SingleRpt/SingleRpt?search_topic=TSN&search_value=547962#null |access-date=2022-04-14 |website=www.itis.gov}}</ref>  

''Plagiomnium cuspidatum'' can commonly be found growing along the base of trees, stumps, coarse woody debris, and rocks in base-rich habitats such as: [[wet meadow]]s, forested rich peatlands, wet forests, fire-dependent woodlands, mesic hardwood forests, and cliff/talus at low to moderate elevations.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |title=Plagiomnium cuspidatum in Flora of North America @ efloras.org |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200001511 |access-date=2022-04-14 |website=www.efloras.org}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> It is commonly used by songbirds and salamanders for nesting material in the wild, and by humans as planting material in bioactive terrariums, aquariums, and paludariums due to their anti- microbial and antifungal properties.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Baby Tooth Moss (Plagiomnium cuspidatum) |url=https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/mosses/plants/bt_moss.html |access-date=2022-04-14 |website=www.illinoiswildflowers.info}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite web |title=Evaluation of Fungicidal Potential of Some Moss Extracts on Phytopathogenic Fungus |url=https://dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/1129775#:~:text=Mosses%20are%20a%20group%20of,%2D%20microbial%2C%20and%20antifungal%20properties.}}</ref> These properties are also being researched for more medicinal uses.

==Description==

===Leaves===
[[File:Plagiomnium_cuspidatum_(d,_143106-475445)_2114.JPG|thumb|216x216px|Close up image of ''P. cuspidatum'' showing sharply toothed edge and noticeable midrib (dark linear area)]]
''Plagiomnium cuspidatum'' has sharp-toothed leaf margins, as its common names suggest, and can be identified from other members of the ''Plagiomnium'' genus by their leaves which measure to about 2.5–3.5 mm in length and have a tip that is tapered more gradually than other ''Plagiomnium'' species, a leaf base that runs all the way down onto the stem, and leaf cells that are elongated and clearly not arranged in diagonal rows.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2013-04-04 |title=Plagiomnium cuspidatum {{!}} BBS Field Guide |url=http://www.bbsfieldguide.org.uk/content/plagiomnium-cuspidatum |access-date=2022-04-14 |archive-date=2013-04-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130404061020/http://www.bbsfieldguide.org.uk/content/plagiomnium-cuspidatum |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref> ''P. cuspidatum'' is often characterized as a small moss with shoots ranging from 1.5-4 cm tall and leaves roughly around 3 mm long.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> Leaves of ''P. cuspidatum'' gradually taper towards the tip, more so than other species in the genus.<ref name=":0" /> Leaf margins are sharply toothed and are absent in the lower half of the leaves while the midrib is obvious.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Ohio Moss and Lichen Association |url=https://ohiomosslichen.org/moss-plagiomnium-cuspidatum/ |website=Ohio Moss and Lichen Association}}</ref> Leaves are arranged in pseudo whorls- where the arrangement of leaves appear to originate at the same level but do not.<ref name=":1" />[[File:Plagiomnium_cuspidatum_114281177.jpg|thumb|160x160px|Up close view of ''P. cuspidatum's'' leaves and stems]]
Using a x20 hand lens, the small cells can be seen to not be in diagonal rows and no longer than wide.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> The non-fertile stems can be one of two descriptions: erect or curved. When aggregated together, the plant forms a green cushion-like structure. When dry, the leaves darken and begin to curl.<ref name=":2" />

===Reproductive structures===
[[File:Plagiomnium_cuspidatum_(e,_145903-474828)_9206.JPG|thumb|203x203px|Capsule and conical lid]]
''Plagiomnium cuspidatum'' do not reproduce asexually but are dioicous – having antheridia and archegonia on separate plants – and synoicous- having archegonia and antheridia on the same plant.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Plagiomnium - FNA |url=http://beta.floranorthamerica.org/Plagiomnium |access-date=2022-04-15 |website=beta.floranorthamerica.org}}</ref> From the foot of the plant, there can be multiple seta that raises the capsules above the plant. Capsules are frequent have a conical lid. Spores range from 18-40μm and are numerous inside the capsule.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":5" />

==Distribution==
''Plagiomnium cuspidatum'' originated in North America, but can now also be found throughout Middle America, Africa, Northern and Southern Asia (excluding China), and Europe. It is widely distributed throughout North America and Europe, but is less commonly found in Africa and Eastern Asia.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last1=Wyatt |first1=Robert |last2=Odrzykoski |first2=Ireneusz J. |date=1998 |title=On the Origins of the Allopolyploid Moss Plagiomnium cuspidatum |journal=The Bryologist |volume=101 |issue=2 |pages=263–271 |doi=10.2307/3244203 |jstor=3244203 |issn=0007-2745}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=NatureServe Explorer 2.0 |url=https://explorer.natureserve.org/Taxon/ELEMENT_GLOBAL.2.125977/Plagiomnium_cuspidatum |access-date=2022-04-14 |website=explorer.natureserve.org}}</ref> Throughout North America, it can be predominantly found in the warmer, humid areas of the continent, though it can still be found and survive in more cool climates as well.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Observations |url=https://inaturalist.ca/observations?locale=en-US&place_id=6712&preferred_place_id=6712&subview=map&taxon_id=141535 |access-date=2022-04-14 |website=iNaturalist Canada |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> 

''Plagiomnium cuspidatum'' is known to be able to use [[artificial light]] to grow in places which are otherwise devoid of natural light, such as [[Crystal Cave (Wisconsin)|Crystal Cave]] in [[Wisconsin]].<ref name="Thatcher 1949">{{cite journal |last1=Thatcher |first1=Edward P. |title=Bryophytes of an Artificially Illuminated Cave |journal=The Bryologist |date=1949 |volume=52 |issue=4 |pages=212–214 |doi=10.2307/3239480 |jstor=3239480 }}</ref>

==Ecology==
Within North America and Europe, ''P. cuspidatum'' is often found growing along the base of trees, stumps, coarse woody debris, and rocks in base-rich habitats such as: [[wet meadow]]s, forested rich peatlands, wet forests, fire-dependent woodlands, mesic hardwood forests, and cliff/talus at low to moderate elevations.<ref name=":10" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" />

The moss is often used by songbirds to make the inner lining of their nest and by [[Four-toed salamander|four-toed salamanders (''Hemidactylium scutatum'')]] when nesting to prevent movement of their eggs.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Baby Tooth Moss (Plagiomnium cuspidatum) |url=https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/mosses/plants/bt_moss.html |access-date=2022-04-15 |website=www.illinoiswildflowers.info}}</ref> Located at the bottom of the mosses, the rhizomes are used by the salamanders to attach their eggs to, which aids in stabilization.<ref name=":6" /> 

==Uses==

===Cultivation===
It can be used as a planting medium in [[Bioactive terrarium|bioactive]] terrariums, aquariums, and paludariums too due to its anti-microbial and antifungal properties.<ref name=":9" /> Its ability to retain high humidity levels and grow in mats or carpets, which provides great cover for the tank's "[[Detritivore|clean-up crew]]", also make it perfect for the hobby.

===Medicinal===
In many bryophytes, there have been antibacterial, antiviral, and antioxidant properties associated with certain species.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=Bryophyte Ecology ebook {{!}} Michigan Technological University Research {{!}} Digital Commons @ Michigan Tech |url=https://digitalcommons.mtu.edu/bryophyte-ecology/ |access-date=2022-04-17 |website=digitalcommons.mtu.edu}}</ref> ''P. cuspidatum'' is able to produce substances that can inhibit bacteria and fungi. But due to these substances being unstable, they have not been able to be used in the medical field but have garnered some attention for its potential use.<ref name=":7" /> The instability of the substance stems from the substance being produced while the moss is under stress and a variety of species produce a variety of substances.<ref name=":7" /> It has been seen that ''P. cuspidatum'' showes resistance to methicillin-resistant ''[[Staphylococcus aureus]],'' commonly known as MRSA.<ref name=":8">{{Cite journal |last1=Vollár |first1=Martin |last2=Gyovai |first2=András |last3=Szűcs |first3=Péter |last4=Zupkó |first4=István |last5=Marschall |first5=Marianna |last6=Csupor-Löffler |first6=Boglárka |last7=Bérdi |first7=Péter |last8=Vecsernyés |first8=Anikó |last9=Csorba |first9=Attila |last10=Liktor-Busa |first10=Erika |last11=Urbán |first11=Edit |date=2018-06-23 |title=Antiproliferative and Antimicrobial Activities of Selected Bryophytes |journal=Molecules (Basel, Switzerland) |volume=23 |issue=7 |article-number=E1520 |doi=10.3390/molecules23071520 |issn=1420-3049 |pmc=6099959 |pmid=29937511|doi-access=free }}</ref> Also, the extracts of ''P. cuspidatum'' studied have shown promising antiproliferative activities against cancer cell lines in which 50% inhibition or more was achieved when testing on cervical, ovarian, and breast cancer cell lines.<ref name=":8" /> The extracts of ''P. cuspidatum,'' flavonoids, have been a topic of interest. Flavonoids are polyphenolic secondary metabolites that are commonly consumed in human diets.<ref name=":8" /> A few of the major flavonoids of ''P. cuspidatum'' are [[saponarin]]e, [[luteolin]], and [[Rhoifolin|apigenin-7''-O''-neohesperidoside]].<ref name=":8" />
